THE JEVONS PRICE INDEX

Compare like with like. Then aggregate.

A Jevons index takes the geometric mean of matched price relatives. Each item must represent the same route, carrier, booking horizon and fare product in the current and base periods.

Match fares→Price relatives→Geometric mean→Route weights
01 / Match the fare item

Use total payable fare, including taxes and required fees. Match cabin, baggage and refund conditions; keep fixed comparison groups so more booking sources do not automatically give an item more weight.

02 / Compute price relatives

For matched item j, divide the current price by that same item's base-period price. Both prices must be positive.

rⱼ = Pⱼ,ₜ / Pⱼ,₀
03 / Apply Jevons

Within route r and horizon h, use n comparable matched items. Logarithms provide a numerically stable geometric mean.

Iᵣ,ₕ = 100 × exp(Σ ln(rⱼ) / n)
04 / Aggregate routes

Use documented PSD route weights that sum to 1. Publish T+1, T+7, T+15, T+30 and T+45 separately. Combine horizons only with authoritative booking-share weights.

Iₙₐₜᵢₒₙₐₗ,ₕ = Σᵣ wᵣ × Iᵣ,ₕ
A WORKED EXAMPLE · ILLUSTRATIVE

Two fares. One comparable basket.

Fare A: ₹5,000 → ₹5,500 gives 1.10. Fare B: ₹4,000 → ₹3,600 gives 0.90.

100 × √(1.10 × 0.90) = 99.50

The basket is about 0.50% below its base period, even though one fare rose. An index of 100 means no overall change.

What this prototype calculates: the dashboard uses one illustrative base fare per route and a geometric mean across available observations. It does not yet match each fare item to its own historical base price or enforce fixed product groups. Route weights are illustrative. Incomplete route coverage returns an unavailable national index. Production publication requires matched historical data, a documented missing-price policy and validation; this is not an official CPI series.

Connect fare observations

Enter your HTTPS collection API. It must allow this site's origin through CORS and return the JSON format below. The endpoint is saved only in this browser; no API keys should be included in its URL.

Expected response format
{"observations": [{
 "id": "unique-id", "route": "DEL-BOM",
 "horizon": 7, "airline": "IndiGo",
 "flight": "6E 101", "source": "IndiGo",
 "fare": 4500, "departureDate": "2026-10-05",
 "observedAt": "2026-09-28T10:00:00Z"
}]}

Supported routes and base fares are listed in Route explorer. Dates must match the selected observation day and horizon. Fetch requests include observation_date and horizons query parameters. Weights remain illustrative until replaced in the project configuration.
